dispatches.title: What Remains
dispatches.subtitle: On Feelings That Cannot Be Captured
dispatches.subject: The Pleasure Dispatch — No. 002: What Remains
dispatches.reflection:
The notion of remembrance has been top of mind as of late.

Not nostalgia exactly. More the strange feeling of looking back at a period of time and realizing that, for whatever reason, you were fully there for it. The Last Resort feels like that to me. I'm grateful for the work I made there, but I'm equally grateful for the time itself. The meals. The conversations. The walks. The slow mornings. Making things without knowing exactly what they would become. Being around other people who were also trying to make sense of something. There is something comforting about knowing that the time was well spent, even if I can't quite explain what came from it.

Since returning to New York, I've been noticing things differently. Recently, I discovered People's NY through a profile in Teeth Magazine. It felt like a breath of fresh air. Not just because of the art, but because of the way the space allows art to actually live. The skylight. The draping. The curtain hooks. The candlelit atmosphere.It feels like an alternative to the white box without having to announce itself as one. An ideal place for a sensual makeout.There was a small painting by Wes Aderhold of distorted busts that held my gaze. I kept returning to it.

Maybe because I've been thinking about something similar in my own work. What I've been pursuing in my photographs are actually feelings that you can't quite depict.

How do you photograph something that can't be captured? Or doesn't want to be depicted?

I've spent years making photographs of figures, objects, surfaces, gestures, and light. Things that are physically there. But increasingly, I'm interested in what exists just outside of the image.

The feeling left behind. The sensation of having been somewhere. The intimacy of a moment that can't be reconstructed. The thing you remember but can't quite describe.

Maybe that's part of what contentment means to me right now, not needing to hold onto everything. Sometimes it is enough to have been there.

To have spent the time well. To remember.

On Feelings That Cannot Be Captured

Maybe that's part of what contentment means to me right now, not needing to hold onto everything. Sometimes it is enough to have been there.

To have spent the time well. To remember.
03 — STUDIO NOTES
I'm still carrying Baltimore with me.

The photographs, paintings, ceramics, and The Pleasure Table are continuing to unfold, but I'm also trying to preserve something less tangible from that time: the feeling of having enough room to notice what was happening.

Maybe that's what I'm really interested in making and protecting.

The world outside of the studio is full of distractions. I find some contentment in knowing that the work will never be a 1:1 representation of the feelings and spaces I'm trying to hold onto, but the effort to get there is worth the journey.

Traces of the feeling that something was pleasurable.

Something happened here.

And I was here to experience it.

What does it mean to preserve a feeling that cannot be photographed, written down, or held?

dispatches.title: Ritual as Pleasure
dispatches.subtitle: Notes on Rhythm, Rest, and Return
dispatches.subject: The Pleasure Dispatch — No. 001: Ritual as Pleasure
dispatches.reflection:
I've been thinking about the difference between ritual and routine.

It started in Miami. I went down to document Kennedy, in the studio, at rest, and ended up paying attention to the small stuff: the pauses, the habits, the way her days had a shape to them. What makes something sustain you, versus something you just do.

I carried that question to Baltimore.

The city had an ease I don't often feel in New York, disparities and all. Greenmount Ave was my main corridor. Mama Koko's was the watering hole. The Coral Wig, the late-night rendezvous. 400 Conejos Reposado, a highlight.

The residency let me settle into my own rhythms.

Breakfast and coffee. Gym. Lunch. Shower. Studio. Dinner. Libation.

Grind Baltimore became part of it fast. A gym only a gym bro could love, honestly, but starting the day in my body before getting into the studio mattered more than I expected. Then the quieter parts: sunrise, the garden, sitting in the sun and letting myself slow down.

In the studio I kept circling the same words. Discipline. Strength. Sensuality. Shame. Balance. Worship. Pleasure.

And one question I couldn't shake: how often do I actually interrogate my own daily pleasures?

Maybe ritual isn't about repeating something. Maybe it's about which things you keep returning to, the coffee, the weights, the shower, the sun, the meal, the drink, the work, the rest, because they give something back.

THE PLEASURE DISPATCH · NO. 001

Ritual as Pleasure

Notes on Rhythm, Rest, and Return
2026-08-31
01 — A REFLECTION
I've been thinking about the difference between ritual and routine.

It started in Miami. I went down to document Kennedy, in the studio, at rest, and ended up paying attention to the small stuff: the pauses, the habits, the way her days had a shape to them. What makes something sustain you, versus something you just do.

The residency let me settle into my own rhythms.

Grind Baltimore became part of it fast. A gym only a gym bro could love, honestly, but starting the day in my body before getting into the studio mattered more than I expected. Then the quieter parts: sunrise, the garden, sitting in the sun and letting myself slow down.

In the studio I kept circling the same words. Discipline. Strength. Sensuality. Shame. Balance. Worship. Pleasure.

Maybe ritual isn't about repeating something. Maybe it's about which things you keep returning to, the coffee, the weights, the shower, the sun, the meal, the drink, the work, the rest, because they give something back.
02 — THE WORK
Surface Tension

I keep thinking about what happens just beneath the surface. With Surface Tension, I’m interested in that space where something is being held, where there’s pressure but nothing has quite given way yet. I think a lot about restraint, desire, and the feeling of wanting to push past that point. There’s something sensual in the waiting, in not knowing when or if something will break. I’m still figuring out what these works are trying to tell me, but I know they keep bringing me back to that feeling of holding and releasing.
03 — STUDIO NOTES
A few of the thoughts, words, and contradictions that followed me through the residency.
04 — PLEASURE NOTES

What have you made a ritual of, and what does that ritual reveal about what you actually desire?

dispatches.title: Welcome to The Pleasure Dispatch
dispatches.subject: The Pleasure Dispatch — No. 000: Welcome to The Pleasure Dispatch
dispatches.reflection: Welcome to the first dispatch. This is a place for notes from the studio, conversations around pleasure, images in progress, and the things I’m thinking about along the way. Less polished statement, more open notebook. I’m interested in what sustains us, what we return to, and what happens when we start paying closer attention to those things. Thanks for being here.
